identity_anchors: stylized letter 'K' formed by thick rounded strokes
disconnected upper-right diagonal stroke of the 'K'
four-pointed star/sparkle symbol at the top right
must_preserve: The specific geometric skeleton of the letter 'K' (vertical bar, lower diagonal, detached upper diagonal)
The rounded caps on all strokes of the 'K'
The four-pointed star shape and its position relative to the 'K'
The negative space gap between the upper diagonal and the rest of the 'K'
can_restyle: Background gradient colors (can be shifted to match theme but should remain dark/contrasting)
Stroke color of the 'K' (can be tinted but must remain high contrast)
Corner radius of the app icon container
Shadow or depth effects on the strokes
must_not_replace_with: Generic fitness icons (dumbbells, hearts, running figures)
Standard serif or sans-serif letter 'K' without the specific detached stroke design
Abstract shapes that do not resemble the letter 'K'
Cute mascots, animals, or cloud shapes
color_preservation: The deep purple is a strong brand identifier; if themed, it should be mapped to a similarly dark, rich hue to maintain the contrast with the white/light logo. The white 'K' can be slightly off-white or tinted, but must remain the lightest element. The star's blue-purple gradient can be adapted to the theme's accent color.
structure_summary: A minimalist, geometric logo featuring a custom rounded 'K' where the top-right arm is detached, accompanied by a sparkle icon on a dark purple field. The identity relies heavily on the specific typography of the 'K' and the purple/white contrast.
risk_notes: Changing the 'K' to a standard font will lose brand recognition immediately.
Removing the detached stroke detail makes it look like a generic initial.
Using a light background without adjusting the logo color will destroy visibility.
Replacing the star with a different shape (like a circle or heart) alters the specific brand vibe.
